summary: Independent backend verification of Phase 1D-c1 (Indian GST engine) only. Wrote a new self-cleaning pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_gst_engine_1dc.py (30 tests, 30 passed) against the live API at http://localhost:3001/api/v1 covering tax-rule CRUD + validation + RBAC, ROOM charge GST snapshot (12% on 15000 -> 1800.00 = CGST 900 + SGST 900, hsnSac 996311, totalRate 12.00 / INTRA_STATE), tariff-slab selection by per-night rate (5000->12%, 9000->18%, exact 7500 boundary inclusive -> 12% while stay total 15000 proves per-unit basis), ship-empty (LAUNDRY -> 0.00 tax + null snapshot), manual auto-GST (F&B 5%) vs explicit taxAmount override (honored verbatim, no snapshot), effective-dating (12% before 2026-09-01, 5% on/after, boundary day inclusive, inactive rule skipped), inter-state single IGST component at full rate, folio totals taxBreakdown aggregation == scalar tax and == sum of line snapshots, amendment reverse+repost NEGATED snapshot (-900/-900, room CGST nets to 1200 after date change), snapshot immutability (editing/deleting the rule leaves historical charges untouched; new charges after delete get 0 tax), specificity/createdAt tie-break, and cents-safe math (components always sum exactly to line taxAmount, verified also as a DB-wide SQL invariant). Ran an exploratory probe script (/tmp/probe_gst.py) that surfaced 4 non-blocking design/validation gaps. Full self-clean confirmed: 0 tax_rules residue for the property, 0 rate plans, 0 leftover reservations for my date windows, 0 inventory invariant violations (sold<0 or sold>capacity).

minor.issue: ROOM GST is resolved against the POSTING date (new Date()) rather than the stay/arrival date: a rule with effectiveFrom 2031-06-01 was NOT applied to a room charge for a 2031-06-05 stay posted today (tax 0.00, snapshot null). For advance bookings the supply date is the stay night, so a rule that becomes effective before check-in is silently ignored (and a mid-stay rate change cannot be represented since ROOM posts one aggregate line for the whole stay). Confirm this is the intended 1D-c1 simplification or switch the chargeDate basis to arrivalDate/per-night.

Negative unitAmount is accepted (e.g. FOOD_AND_BEVERAGE -500.00 -> amount -500.00) and GstService clamps taxable to max(0, ...), so the negative line reduces the subtotal but carries 0.00 tax — GST is not symmetric for credit-style lines. DTO doc says 'positive; use DISCOUNT type' but there is no validator enforcing it.
Explicit taxAmount override accepts negatives (taxAmount '-50.00' stored verbatim, 201). No lower bound / sanity check on the manual tax override.

No overlap/uniqueness guard: two rules for the same (property, chargeType, effectiveFrom) with identical specificity but different rates are both accepted (12% and 18%); resolution silently falls back to latest createdAt. Deterministic but easy to misconfigure — consider rejecting or flagging overlapping slabs/dates.

Read permission is SettingsView OR BookingsView (readonly@stayos.local can list rules) — slightly wider than the stated SettingsView-only scope. Writes correctly require SettingsManage (readonly -> 403).

Odd rates split into halves can under-collect 1 paisa vs the scalar rate: 5% of 333.33 -> CGST 8.33 + SGST 8.33 = 16.66 while 5% exact is 16.67. Components-sum design keeps the line internally consistent (verified), but the effective rate on such lines is marginally below the configured rate; acceptable only if intentional.

action_items: Decide/document the ROOM GST effective-date basis (posting date vs stay date) — currently a rule effective before check-in but after today is not applied to advance bookings.
Add validation for negative unitAmount and negative explicit taxAmount on POST folio charges (or explicitly support credit lines with negated GST).
Consider an overlap guard (or a documented deterministic precedence) for tax rules with identical chargeType/effectiveFrom/specificity.
critical_code_review_comments: gst.service.ts resolveRule() loads all active rules for (property, chargeType) and filters in JS — fine at current volumes, but the effectiveFrom/slab filter should eventually move into the SQL WHERE clause for large rule sets.

billing.service.ts generateRoomChargesFromSnapshot() uses `slabBasisAmount: unitCents/100` derived from grandTotal/nights (an AVERAGE per-night). With per-night differential pricing the slab match may straddle two slabs; a per-night breakdown from snapshot.nights would be more accurate.
billing.service.ts is 606 lines and approaching the 700-line split threshold; the GST/tax-snapshot helpers (toStoredSnapshot/negateTaxSnapshot) are good candidates to extract.
No cross-property leakage found: tax-rule endpoints are property-scoped (unknown property -> 404, malformed uuid -> 400) and responses contain no internal ids beyond uuids.
seed_data_creation: Temporary only: 3 ACTIVE rate plans (T1GSTL 5000/night default, T1GSTH 9000/night, T1GSTE 7500/night), ~7 tax rules (ROOM slabs 12/18, F&B 5, MINIBAR 18, SPA 12 + 5 effective-dated, transient MISC rules) and 6 CONFIRMED reservations in 2031-03/04 with folios. All removed in session teardown; residue counts verified zero.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable GST regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_gst_engine_1dc.py (self-cleaning, date window 2031-03-02..2031-04-30, TAG=T1GST). It creates its own rate plans + tax rules per session, so do not run it concurrently with other billing suites (tax rules are property-global and would change other suites' tax expectations). Pre-existing unrelated reservation residue exists at arrival dates 2031-05-07 / 2031-06-01 / 2031-06-21 from earlier iterations. Phase 1D-c1 verified functionally correct; only design/validation gaps listed above remain open.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found in the 1D-c1 slice. The ROOM effective-date observation roots in billing.service.ts:156 passing `chargeDate: new Date()` to GstService.computeTax, so rule resolution uses posting time rather than the stay period; the negative-amount observations root in create-folio-charge.dto.ts using @IsNumberString() without a positivity constraint combined with GstService clamping taxableCents with Math.max(0, ...).
